status.comment:
Felix 2026-10-16: back to full flow to the children, pouring intrinsic value in each step, normalizing each iteration; units per project (meta.costUnit already exists, default ''). Claude's objection: the exact solve already is the limit of 'pour intrinsic, flow to children' iterations, normalized once. Normalizing every iteration adds a hidden per-hop discount, the issue of 6e1b0b0e. 'Full flow' maps to self weight 0 everywhere: drop loopWeight by migration (today 496 ideas have 1, 228 have 0, 80 unset), so only leaves realize value. Question: drop self weight and keep the one-shot solve?

Outcome: Per-iteration normalization settles at a factor of 1.651 per iteration: a hidden per-hop discount of 0.606. Against the one-shot full flow, every idea's value shrinks to between 0.048 and 0.606 (median 0.222), the deeper the less. The ranking stays similar (Spearman 0.978, top-20 overlap 18). Dropping self weight barely moves aggregated values (Spearman 0.994 vs current) but changes the top 20 noticeably (overlap 11). Effectiveness: Turns the objection into numbers: the per-iteration variant is the one-shot model plus a graph-dependent depth discount of about 0.6 per hop, which favors shallow ideas. Lesson: If a depth discount is wanted, make it an explicit, named knob (6e1b0b0e) rather than a side effect of normalization, whose size changes whenever the graph changes.
